phases.name: Full S2R
phases.short: The SoC powers down, DRAM in self-refresh
phases.summary: Aura’s `SYSTEM_SUSPEND` gains the SoC steps in macOS’s order. Five `slpa` runs (11-04 and 11-05) came back on the alarm with the storage controller dead and the SoC AWAKE throughout. Image 52 then added macOS’s PMGR S2R timer and its all-core deep sleep: the timer is the first PMGR write the SoC acts on, resetting the Mac about 60 s later unless the S2R entry completes, and it does not complete even with every core powered down (runs D to F). The rest of macOS’s PMGR quiesce (clock gates, PLL-off, GPU) is next.

pieces.name: Timed wake
pieces.known: The PMU RTC alarm on SPMI irq 2, AIC 724. The “fired” bit must be cleared before re-arming. Upstream’s alarm is T6030-only, so the T602x patches are still needed.
pieces.next: Shape it for upstream; power-on from off is untested

pieces.name: Boot CPU hand-back
pieces.known: `SYSTEM_SUSPEND` returns through the kernel’s `cpu_resume`, 20 of 20 on all CPUs (image 48). It works with retention through `deep_wfi()`; an inline `dsb sy; isb; wfi` never woke (images 37 to 40). Powered down without retention, the core never re-enters at RVBAR (images 32 to 36).
pieces.next: A real S2R wake comes back through RVBAR; image 51 resumes the kernel from there, not reached yet

pieces.name: Wake sources
pieces.known: Deep WFI with AIC lines 724 (alarm) and 865 (SMC mailbox) unmasked. The power key wakes on 865.
pieces.next: Lid; stop the SMC’s early `Elec Cause` syslog wakes

pieces.name: AIC
pieces.known: Save and mask every bank, restore on resume (syscore). It runs on every Phase 2 cycle. Because it masks everything, wake detection has to come from the PMU/SMC side.

pieces.name: SMC handshake
pieces.known: `WKTP` and `slpw` are harmless. `slpa` makes the SMC cut the storage controller’s (ANS) power: in five runs inside a real suspend with all CPUs off (2026-11-04 and 05) the Mac resumed on the alarm and the ANS never booted again. On its own `slpa` does not start the SoC’s sleep (PMGR counters: `AWAKE` throughout). The dead-man switch’s reboot brings the disk back every time. `SetAPPower` IDLE to the SMC is acked and safe.
pieces.next: The SoC sleep after `slpa` (runs C, G, H); the ANS's power-on ack should follow a real S2R wake

pieces.name: PMP
pieces.known: IDLE works in s2idle (acks in about 400 us) and now after `slpa` too (run C again, 2026-11-05 21:22: accepted, no crash; the 16:01 crash was the test kernel’s double `SetAPPower`). The wake from IDLE fails without a power cycle (-62). The display requests are released for sleep in normal suspends; once the PMP is IDLE the release is refused (`-EALREADY`), so it has to move before `slpa`. A PMGR reset of `ps_pmp` crashes the SoC. Since 2026-11-06 the test kernel can withdraw every request (the displays and ISP_SYS) just before `slpa`, while the PMP still acks (`deep_steps` 32, run Q: 0xf000 to 0, back after the wake); in C, I, J and L the noirq release came after the IDLE and was refused.
pieces.next: Its wake after a real S2R (run L first)

pieces.name: AOP
pieces.known: macOS tells the AOP the AP is asleep (RTKit `SetAPPower` 0x201) and leaves it running; before that `AppleSPU::_stopQueue` stops each endpoint's queue (`0xa4`, ack `0x87`), and `_startQueue` starts it on wake (`0xa3`, ack `0x86`). Sent alone, the 0x201 crashed the AOP in its ring writer. The test kernel now does the whole handshake, with the 0x201 before `slpa` as macOS. The queues must run again before the secondary CPUs come back (stopped, every incoming core hung in the kernel's secondary entry), so they restart from syscore resume. 4 of 4 suspend cycles with all 10 CPUs back, the sensors live (2026-11-06 00:00). In run J (2026-11-06 15:18, with `slpa`, the PMP's IDLE and the whole quiesce) the queues stopped 12 of 12 and the 0x201 was acked; the S2R timer still reset at 86 s.
pieces.next: Nothing new until the S2R entry completes

pieces.name: Secondary CPUs
pieces.known: CPU_OFF parks the core in Aura’s retention deep WFI loop; CPU_ON hands it back through the spin table, with `CYC_OVRD` restored first. 20 of 20 suspend cycles with all nine.
pieces.next: Runtime hotplug outside suspend; RVBAR re-entry after real power loss

pieces.name: PMGR quiesce, S2R timer
pieces.known: The S2R timer (1 to MPMGR_AON + 0x4000) works from Aura: it resets the SoC about 60 s after the write unless the S2R entry completes. With `slpa`, every core powered down macOS’s way and all of `quiesceHW` but the cluster power-off (image 53, runs G and H), it still resets at about 85 s after `echo mem`. Adding the PMP’s IDLE in the same sleep (run I) changes nothing. The last `quiesceHW` step, the soc-cluster power-off (`enableCluster`: the ADT's `soc-clusters` at `0x28e088000`), is image 54's aura-ctl 16: unattended on 2026-11-06 the ANE and AVE clusters powered fully off and the P-core and display clusters stayed pending; all 10 CPUs came back. Run J (2026-11-06 15:18, owner-attended) did every macOS step found so far in one sleep (`slpa`, the PMP's IDLE, the AOP handshake, the whole `quiesceHW` with the clusters, every core down): reset 86 s after `echo mem`, the timer again. Every timer run (D to J) left the PMGR's AP wake mask at Linux's all-zero value, i.e. every wake source enabled; macOS enables 22. Runs L and M (J with macOS's wake mask, 2026-11-06) ended in the 120 s dog, but a check run with a mask of 0 did too: the mask step in `suspend_late` breaks the suspend by itself, so L and M most likely never reached `slpa` or the timer. The mask step works since 2026-11-06 16:04 (`ioremap_np`; the earlier posted mapping stalled the bus), and macOS's own mask lets the PMU alarm wake Aura's deep WFI with the SoC up. Run L again with the mask really set (2026-11-06 16:11): the timer's reset at 86 s, as J. Run N (2026-11-06 16:31: L with the PMP's requests at 0 before `slpa`, as macOS): 86 s again. Run R (2026-11-06 16:41, image 55: also each secondary's PMGR stop request, the last step in macOS's trace): 86 s again.
pieces.next: Static: the PMGR power domains Linux leaves on at sleep (ps_* still on at suspend_late) against what macOS has off

findings.title: The AOP's queues must run before the CPUs come back
findings.body: With the AOP's endpoint queues stopped across the CPU bring-up, every secondary hung in the kernel's secondary entry after Aura handed it the entry (5 runs); restarting them from syscore resume, before the secondaries, fixed it (3 runs, 12 cycles).

findings.title: The gap is SoC sleep itself
findings.body: Awake idle matches macOS once the PMP runs (5.38 W against 5.57 W, SoC 1.22 W on both). The lid-closed gap is not the devices.

findings.title: s2idle’s 1.4 W is power left on, not wakes
findings.body: The 3.2 wakes a second come from the AOP’s ambient-light and lid-angle reports and cost milliwatts. The PMP doesn’t change the drain.

findings.title: macOS tells the PMP when the system sleeps
findings.body: Read from the macOS 13.5 kernelcache: the full order of sleep and quiesce actions, the SMC `MBSE` handshake, PMGR’s last write, and the PMP’s RTKit IDLE (0x201), which is Linux’s unused `apple_rtkit_idle()`.

findings.title: `slpa` takes the storage away
findings.body: After `slpa` every NVMe access fails: in s2idle (10-22) and in five real suspends (11-04 and 05), where the Mac resumed on the alarm and the storage controller never booted again. A reboot from Linux (the dead-man switch’s) brings it back. On its own `slpa` does not put the SoC to sleep, so it cannot be the last step by itself.

findings.title: The PMP’s wake from IDLE is a power cycle
findings.body: RUN alone woke it 0 of 3. Gating its SRAM did not restart it, and resetting `ps_pmp` crashed the SoC. `ps_pmp` is pinned on by iBoot.

findings.title: ISR_EL1 is blind at EL2 under VHE
findings.body: With IMO/FMO set, Aura saw only the virtual pending state. The fix was to watch the AIC’s HW_STATE for the alarm line.

findings.title: The kernel masks the whole AIC for suspend
findings.body: `aic_syscore_suspend` masks every line, as macOS does. In real S2R the wake must be detected from the PMU/SMC side.

findings.title: A core powered down without retention doesn’t come back on an IRQ
findings.body: Across images 32 to 36 the boot core never re-entered at RVBAR. Secondaries only return through a PMGR CPU-start written by another core.

findings.title: NVMe drops cached writes on a hard reset
findings.body: The ANS firmware caches until a clean `saveCtx` shutdown. That explained the lost logs and the filesystem damage after hotplug hangs.

findings.title: The PMU RTC alarm is the timed wake
findings.body: Linux had no driver for the alarm macOS uses for dark wakes. `rtcwake -m freeze -s 30` woke after about 31 s, 3 of 3.

findings.title: Parked cores need retention, and must not keep WFI_MODE 3
findings.body: The October hotplug deaths came from two things: the CPU_OFF park powered cores down without retention, and a re-onlined core inherited `CYC_OVRD` WFI_MODE 3 from the park. With both fixed, all nine secondaries go off and come back every suspend cycle.

findings.title: A CPU_OFF that never returns leaks a preempt count
findings.body: The kernel’s EFI call path disables preemption around the firmware call. A successful CPU_OFF never comes back, so the re-onlined core started with one count too many (“scheduling while atomic”, once per core per cycle). Fixed in the test kernel.

findings.title: `slpa` alone does not put the SoC to sleep
findings.body: With every CPU in Aura and the boot core in deep WFI, `slpa` still left the SoC running. On the wake `waka` is acked, but the storage controller never acks its power-on (`IOP power acknowledgment failed: -62`). macOS does more between `slpa` and the power-down: `SetAPPower` and `SetIOPPower` to the PMP, the CPU stops and the PCPM clears.

findings.title: A live kernel with no disk is not a hang
findings.body: After the `slpa` run the watchdogs saw a healthy kernel, so nothing reset the Mac for about 15 min. Unattended `slpa` runs need a dead-man switch tied to the disk.

findings.title: The watchdog cannot cover a long sleep by itself
findings.body: WD1 counts 32 bits at 24 MHz, about 178 s at most. Aura now wakes on the EL2 physical timer every 60 s, re-arms the dog and sleeps again, so suspends of any length keep the safety net.

findings.title: Parking the CPUs alone saves almost nothing
findings.body: Suspend to RAM with every CPU in Aura’s deep WFI drew 1.365 W over 30 min on battery, and `s2idle` 1.390 and 1.413 W in the same boot. The gap to macOS’s 0.24 W is the SoC and DRAM staying up, which only the SoC steps (`slpa` and after) can close.

findings.title: A PMGR gate alone does not lose the storage controller
findings.body: genpd switched `ps_ans2` (the ANS, its mailbox and its SART) off in each of last night’s 4 suspends, and NVMe came back every time. So `slpa` takes away more than that gate does, perhaps the rail itself. The SART’s entries (8 of 16 used) are the first thing to check after the next `slpa` run.

findings.title: macOS writes the storage controller’s SART back on every start
findings.body: `IOSARTMapper::_setActive(true)` (13.5) copies the SART’s 16 config and 16 address words the first time, and writes them back every later time. The ANS start after sleep runs it. So macOS expects the SART to lose its entries in S2R, and the Linux SART driver had nothing for that. The test kernel now does the same.

findings: macOS tells the PMU the AP is asleep (`IOPMUBootStage` 0x50) in its sleep action, and gives the SMC a 10 s AP-watchdog deadline at the last quiesce step; Linux leaves 0x30 (“OS running”) through suspend, so a reset from sleep counts as a boot error

The PMGR’s AP wake-source mask (`0x29e00400c`, 1 = disabled) is 0 under Linux. macOS’s value, with only its 22 sources enabled, also stops the alarm and the EL2 timer from waking the boot CPU out of Aura’s deep WFI

The PMGR keeps per-state time counters (`AWAKE`, `SLP_S2R`, `SYS_S2R_AOP`, …), off under Linux. Turned on, they show the SoC stays AWAKE through Aura’s suspend and s2idle; in an `slpa` run that comes back they can prove a real S2R
PMGR counters after `slpa` plus the PMP steps (run C, 2026-11-05): `AWAKE` the whole 65 s, `SLP_S2R` 0. `slpa` does not put the SoC to sleep by itself; it only takes the storage controller down
The SART is intact after `slpa` (run C: `entries kept across suspend`); the ANS failure after `slpa` has another cause

The PMGR’s S2R timer (1 to MPMGR_AON + 0x4000, macOS’s `startS2RTimer`) resets the SoC about 60 s after it is written unless the S2R entry completes, whatever the alarm does (runs D, D2; 2026-11-05). With every core powered down macOS’s way it still resets (run E); the cores alone end in a WD1 reset (run F)

Apple coprocessors boot from an IO RVBAR in their ASC wrapper (`0x347050000` for the ANS, `0x28e850000` for the PMP), set and locked by iBoot; macOS rewrites it on every CPU start (`AppleASCWrapV4::_setIORVBAR`), Linux never does. It survives a normal suspend with `ps_ans2` gated and `slpa` too (run A, 2026-11-05 18:04), so it is not why the ANS fails after `slpa`

findings.title: The PMP crash was ours
findings.body: After `slpa` the PMP firmware crashed because the test kernel told it the AP’s sleep state twice; the firmware panics when given the state it already has. One request, as macOS sends, is the fix. The PMP still holds display and ISP requests that macOS releases before `slpa`.

findings.title: The storage controller does start after `slpa`
findings.body: Its firmware answers the first handshake but never acknowledges power-on, and its boot address and SART are intact. It most likely waits on the storage power the SMC cut, which a real S2R wake would restore. So the SoC sleep comes first.

findings.title: The PMP lets the displays go for sleep
findings.body: Withdrawing the three display requests in suspend and asserting them on resume works in a normal suspend; the PMP acks both. That puts the PMP close to macOS’s state at `slpa`; only ISP’s request differs.

findings.title: What we have now sleeps at 1.46 W
findings.body: An hour each on battery in one boot: suspend to RAM through Aura 1.458 W, s2idle 1.504 W, macOS 0.24 W. Parking the CPUs and releasing the display requests barely matter while the SoC stays up; the gap is the SoC sleep itself.

findings.title: macOS’s whole PMGR quiesce is not enough on its own
findings.body: With `slpa`, every core powered down and all of `quiesceHW` but the cluster power-off before the S2R timer, the SoC still resets 85 s later (runs G, H). The PMP now accepts its sleep request (run C). The next test does both in one sleep, as macOS does.

findings.title: Every macOS step found so far leaves the S2R entry incomplete
findings.body: `slpa`, the PMP's IDLE, the AOP's sleep handshake, the whole PMGR quiesce (clusters included) and every core powered down, all in one sleep (run J, 2026-11-06), still end in the S2R timer's reset at about 85 s. Not yet combined with them: macOS's PMGR wake mask (Linux enables every wake source; a pending one may hold the entry).

findings.title: The wake-mask step in suspend_late breaks the suspend by itself
findings.body: Writing the PMGR's AP wake mask from `suspend_late` ends in the 120 s dog even when the value is 0 (check run, 2026-11-06 15:44). So runs L and M (macOS's mask with `slpa` and the S2R timer) most likely stopped there, before `slpa`; they do not show that macOS's mask stops the timer or blocks every wake. The step now runs from the PM notifier.

findings.title: The PMGR wake mask needs a non-posted mapping; macOS's own mask keeps the alarm wake
findings.body: Every module access to the wake mask with a posted `ioremap()` stalled the SoC fabric (the DT's `/soc` is `nonposted-mmio`), so runs L and M and the 11-05 mask runs never tested a mask. With `ioremap_np()` the mask is written before the AOP's sleep message and restored on wake, and with macOS's 22 sources the PMU alarm still wakes Aura's deep WFI (2026-11-06 16:08). With the mask set, run L (every macOS step found so far) still ends in the S2R timer's reset at 86 s, so the mask is not what the entry waits for.

findings.title: The PMP's requests at 0 before slpa change nothing either
findings.body: Run N (2026-11-06 16:31) did L with the PMP's display and ISP requests released before `slpa`, so the PMP went IDLE with nothing requested, as in macOS: the S2R timer's reset at 86 s, as before. Next from macOS's trace: the PMGR stop request for each secondary core (image 55).

findings.title: Every step of macOS's sleep trace together still ends in the S2R timer's reset
findings.body: Run R (2026-11-06 16:41) did slpw, the PMP's requests at 0, slpa, the PMU boot stage, macOS's wake mask, the AOP handshake, the SMC's and PMP's IDLE, the whole quiesceHW with the clusters, the S2R timer, the secondaries' stop requests and every core in deep sleep, in macOS's order: reset at 86 s. What is left is the devices: Linux leaves PMGR power domains on that macOS has off by then.

findings.title: dwc3-apple oopses when a never-connected USB-C port is unbound
findings.body: Run U (2026-11-06 17:00): `dwc3_apple_remove()` takes its lock through `platform_get_drvdata()`, which only `dwc3_core_probe()` sets on the first cable event, so unbinding a port with no cable since boot dereferences NULL (+0x5b0). The unbind runs now skip ports without an xHCI. Ports with a cable are syscore devices by design, so their `atc*_usb` domain stays on in every suspend.

findings.title: Unbinding a device keeps its PM domains on (DEFER_OFF)
findings.body: Run U2 (2026-11-06 17:11) unbound the display stack and a USB-C port and came back on the alarm, but only the PMP's display domains went off (96 of 200 still on). The PMGR driver gives every domain that is on at boot GENPD_FLAG_DEFER_OFF, so genpd keeps a domain on while any DT consumer has no bound driver, and ACTIVE_WAKEUP keeps it on for a device on a wakeup path. The next step is a per-domain dump of why each one is held.

findings.title: Why Linux keeps 19 PM domains on at sleep
findings.body: Run S3 (2026-11-06 17:18) printed genpd's reason per domain: the three DCPs put themselves on a wake path in suspend (the driver says it cannot fully shut the DCP down yet), which holds 13 display domains including afr; the USB-C controllers are syscore while their core is up, or have wakeup enabled (3 domains); sio and the apcie_gp pair stay on for DT always-on children. Whether the PMGR's S2R entry waits for them is the next test.

findings.title: Turning the held display and USB-C domains off in Aura hangs a normal suspend
findings.body: Run Y (2026-11-06 17:31): with Aura switching the 12 domains Linux keeps on (the three display chains, the three USB-C ports) off before its wait and back on after, the normal-path suspend ended in the 120 s watchdog; without that step it comes back. Either the writes stall the fabric or Linux's resume hangs on devices that lost their state. Image 57 lets each group be tested alone (runs Y1 to Y3).

findings.title: Turning the USB-C domains off from Aura stalls the SoC; the S2R timer works without slpa
findings.body: Runs Y1T and T0 (2026-11-06 17:48 and 17:54): the S2R timer alone resets the SoC about 85 s after echo mem on a normal suspend, but written after the USB-C domain-off step it never fires (145 s, the watchdog). Aura stalls in that step, most likely because the USB controllers keep running through the suspend (syscore xHCI) and losing their power wedges the fabric. They must be stopped by Linux first.

findings.title: Aura cannot force the held domains off; Linux must quiesce them first
findings.body: Run Y2T (2026-11-06 17:59): the external displays' domains (nothing attached) off from Aura, then the S2R timer: WD1 at 145 s, as Y1T for USB-C. Aura stalls in the domain-off step whenever the domain's devices are still running (DCP firmware, syscore xHCI). The held domains must be powered off by genpd after their drivers stop the devices (USB-C wake paths and xHCI; DCP RTKit shutdown and cold start), then the S2R entry is tried with them off.

findings.title: With wakeup off, genpd powers an idle USB-C port's domain off; live ports are held as syscore
findings.body: Run S4 (2026-11-06 18:08): disabling power/wakeup on the dwc3-apple devices let genpd turn atc1_usb (no cable) off in noirq and on again at resume (98 of 200 domains on, S3 99; back on the alarm in 32.8 s). atc0_usb (charger, device mode) and atc2_usb (xHCI with a receiver) stay on because dwc3-apple marks a port with its core up as syscore. Next: tear such ports down before a deep suspend and bring them up after it.

findings.title: A deep-suspend teardown in dwc3-apple frees every USB-C domain; USB comes back
findings.body: Run S5 (2026-11-06 18:17): with dwc3_apple.test_deep_teardown (stop a live core at PM_SUSPEND_PREPARE as a cable removal would, restart it in its role at PM_POST_SUSPEND) and phy_apple_atc.test_restore_pd_off (the T8103-table PHY restores itself after its domain was off), atc0_usb and atc2_usb go off in sleep: 96 of 200 domains on (S3 99). Back on the alarm in 32.7 s; the receiver re-enumerated and the charger port is in device mode again. Left: the three DCP chains (13 domains, wake path by design) and two always-on groups.

findings.title: With the DCP firmware shut down, genpd turns every device-held domain off: 83 of 200 on
findings.body: Run S6 (2026-11-06 21:19): appledrm.test_sleep_off shuts each DCP's RTKit firmware down in suspend instead of claiming the wake path; with the USB-C teardown all 13 display domains and 3 USB-C domains go off in noirq. At syscore suspend 83 of 200 domains are on (S3 99): the DT's always-on ones plus sio and the apcie_gp pair, held by always-on children. Back on the alarm in 32.8 s; the DCPs stay dead (not restarted yet) and the GPU's gfx domain failed to power on at resume (new).

findings.title: With every device-held domain off, the S2R entry still ends in the timer's reset
findings.body: Run R6 (2026-11-06 21:26): run R's full macOS sleep sequence (slpa, SetAPPower, quiesceHW, the S2R timer, CPU stop requests, deep sleep) plus S6's Linux-side domain-offs (83 of 200 on): the next kernel came 86.0 s after echo mem, the timer's reset, as in R. The devices' power domains are not what the PMGR's S2R entry waits for. Left from the macOS trace: the PMP's CPU-complex requests (PCPM0/1), which macOS clears after slpa and Linux never asserts.

findings.title: The PMP acknowledges CPU-complex (PCPM0/1) requests from Linux
findings.body: Run S7 (2026-11-06 21:36): pmp_report.test_pcpm 0x300 asserted at PM_SUSPEND_PREPARE (request and ack 0xf300) and withdrawn after the wake (0xf000), each acknowledged; a normal suspend came back as before. Run R7 (the same withdrawn after slpa and the PMP's IDLE, as macOS's trace step 6) waits for an attended first run.

findings.title: The GPU domain hangs off afr, which went off for the first time in S6
findings.body: gfx has parents gpx (always-on) and afr; afr's other child is dispext0_sys. With the display chain off (S6), afr powered off, and at resume gfx did not reach its on state (BUSY, actual 0). afr may need state restored after a power-off, or gfx the PMP's GFX request.

findings.title: afr going off breaks the GPU's power-up after sleep
findings.body: Run S8 (2026-11-06 21:41): S6 with pmgr_pwrstate.test_sleep_keep=afr (84 of 200 on): the GPU's gfx domain powered up after the wake without error, unlike S6. afr, gfx's parent, comes back from a power-off without what gfx needs. Test runs keep afr on; a real S2R needs the GPU bring-up to cope with afr having lost power.

findings.title: AMCC errors DSID_AGE_OUT and UNEXP_RT_HIT_DIR are enabled and pending before the commit
findings.body: Run G58 (2026-11-06 22:30, image 58 records): every one of the 4 AMCC instances has error status word 0 bit 26 (DSID_AGE_OUT) and word 1 bit 8 (UNEXP_RT_HIT_DIR) set, both enabled (plane 0 enables 0xb7bffdfd / 0x3f00), on the normal path just before Aura's wait. On T8140 (DJ) exactly this wakes the SoC within 20 ms of the S2R commit when no platform error handler runs; macOS clears the enables at quiesce. R8 clears them (aura-ctl 0x200).

findings.title: WD2 sits at a 90 s alarm, disabled, counter running
findings.body: Run G58: WD2 (WDT + 0x20) alarm 0x80befc00 = 90 s, ctl 0, counter running (about 87 s at entry); iBoot's leftover, as on the M1 (Naeem, try28). WD1 is Aura's 120 s suspend dog. Whether the S2R timer's reset about 60 s after its write is WD2 is run W1's question.

findings.title: WD2 is involved in the reset after the S2R timer, but is not the only one
findings.body: Run W1 (2026-11-06 22:34): the S2R timer with WD2 stopped 100 ms later reset about 116 s after echo mem, not 85 s (T0) or 145 s (WD1). The 30 s alarm did not resume Linux. Next: image 59 resumes the kernel right after the timer so Linux can log the watchdogs until the reset.

findings.title: Clearing the AMCC error enables and masking the AIC does not complete the entry
findings.body: Run R8 (2026-11-06 22:41, owner attended): R7 (every macOS step found, slpa, PCPM0/1, devices off, afr kept) plus the AMCC DSID_AGE_OUT/UNEXP_RT_HIT_DIR enables cleared before the S2R timer and every AIC line masked after it: the timer's reset at 86 s again. Next: the CPU-complex power gates and CLLT writes that the t8103 and T8140 entries have and Aura does not.

findings.title: After the S2R timer is written, Linux cannot be resumed
findings.body: Run W2 (2026-11-06 23:01, image 59, aura-ctl 0x2101): the S2R timer, then Aura returned straight to the kernel (the same psci_resume_kernel as a normal wake, without the wait). Linux printed nothing more, its network never came back, and the next kernel started 86 s after echo mem, the timer's usual reset. W1 showed Aura's own code still runs at least 100 ms after the timer, so the CPU and DRAM keep working, but the kernel's resume does not get through. The timer write is the point of no return; the watchdogs after it cannot be logged from Linux.

findings.title: Aura's armed WD1 does not keep the S2R entry from completing
findings.body: Run R9 (2026-11-06 23:08, owner attended): R8 (every macOS step found, slpa, PCPM0/1, devices off, afr kept, AMCC errors cleared, AIC masked) plus WD1 disarmed right before the S2R timer, so every AON watchdog but WD2 is off at the commit as in macOS: the next kernel 86 s after echo mem, the timer's reset again.

findings.title: The PMU marks the AP asleep at the timer reset
findings.body: boot-error-stage (PMU 0x6003) reads 0x50 after the timer resets of every run that sent macOS's slpa and SetAPPower 0x201 (I, J, L, N, R, R6, R8, R9) and 0x30 after every other kind of boot. Linux never writes it, so the SMC/PMU firmware sets it on the AP-sleep messages: the SMC side considers the AP asleep, and the missing part is on the SoC side.

findings.title: The PMU has free scratch that Aura can write
findings.body: 13.5's AppleDialogSPMIPMU uses legacy scratch keys 0-3, 8-11, 0xf, 0x18-0x1a and 0x1f (base 0x6000). Keys 4-7, 0xc-0xe, 0x10-0x17 and 0x1b-0x1e are unused; 0x6004 takes a write from Linux and reads it back. Image 60 puts Aura's stage codes there.

findings.title: The boot core gets through Aura's whole sleep tail
findings.body: Run R10 (image 60b, 2026-11-06 23:43): PMU scratch 0x6004 = 0x18 after the 86 s timer reset. Aura wrote the timer, stopped WD2, masked the AIC and released the secondaries, and reached the point before its cache flush and deep WFI. It never returned from the WFI and never came back through RVBAR.

findings.title: Naeem Malik's M1 sleeps once the last core reaches its WFI
findings.body: malik-na/m1-power-lab (11-06/07): his ~5 s post-commit resets came from his own last core hanging on an MMIO access to a clock-parked USB controller. With no hardware access after the commit (try32) the M1 really slept, woke on the RTC alarm at the locked RVBAR, and held 0.05 W over 3 hours (try46).

findings.title: At the last moment one P complex is still on
findings.body: Run R11 (image 60c, 2026-11-07 06:29): the boot core reached its deep WFI (code 0x19) and the PMP's requests were all released (0), but 2 ms after the secondaries' release the PCPM0 power word was still on while PCPM1 was off. Aura's park loop never acks the release IPI (IPI_SR), so released secondaries may spin instead of powering down.

findings.title: With IPI_SR cleared both P complexes power down; E core 3 does not sleep
findings.body: Run R12 (image 60d, 2026-11-07 06:36): the boot core reached its deep WFI again, PCPM0 and PCPM1 both read actual state 0 and PACC0/1 bit 4 cleared, so the release-IPI ack fixed R11's lit P complex. Every P core and E cores 1-2 reached the S2R sleep; E core 3 (MPIDR 3) never did. The timer still reset the Mac at 86 s.

findings.title: cpu3 gets the release IPI but never leaves its park WFI
findings.body: Run R13 (image 60e, 2026-11-07 06:48): Aura held cpus 1-6 and 8-10 as CPU_OFF and sent each the release IPI; all but cpu3 reached the S2R sleep. cpu3 was CPU_OFF too. Both P complexes were off within 6 ms. The timer still reset the Mac at 86 s.

findings.title: Nothing wakes cpu3 from its park WFI at the release
findings.body: Run R14 (image 60f, 2026-11-07 06:55): cpu3 was sent the release IPI at its own MPIDR, had entered its park loop once, and never came out of that WFI, not even for a second IPI 2 ms later. cpus 1 and 2 on the same path wake. Suspects, all done to the E cluster before the release: the CPUSTART stop request (aura-ctl bit 5), the cluster targets and the clock parking.

findings.title: Without the CPUSTART stop request every core reaches its final deep sleep
findings.body: Run R15 (image 60f, aura-ctl 0x5b1f, 2026-11-07 07:02): without Aura's per-core CPUSTART+0 stop request before the release IPI, cpu3 slept too. All 9 secondaries were in cpu_sleep(true), the boot core reached its deep WFI and both P complexes were off. The SoC still did not sleep: timer reset at 86 s. Next: no hardware access after the commit (image 60g).

findings.title: Naeem's quiet commit alone does not finish the entry; Aura never turned off the boot cluster
findings.body: Run R16 (image 60g, aura-ctl 0xdb1f, 2026-11-07 07:09): every hardware access before the S2R timer, the timer written three times, nothing after it but the flush and deep WFI; every core slept, both P complexes off; still the 86 s reset. Static: 13.5's AppleT6020PMGR::quiesceHW turns off logical clusters from 1, and the ADT soc-clusters byte 3 makes cluster 1 EACC (the boot cluster), 2 PACC0, 3 PACC1. Image 54 used byte 0 and never wrote EACC; R16's snapshot shows EACC target 0xf. The M1 entry also writes both CPU complexes off before the commit. Image 60h adds it (R17).

findings.title: With EACC off too the entry still does not finish; the SEP is never told to sleep
findings.body: Run R17 (image 60h, aura-ctl 0x1db1f, 2026-11-07 07:22): EACC's target reached 0, all else as R16; still the 86 s reset. The CPU-complex PS words read target 0 even awake. 13.5's AppleSEPManager::_sleepSEPAsync sends the SEP a SLEEP control message (EP 0, opcode 0x0c, type 2) before system sleep; Linux's apple-sep never does. Testing it touches SEP state shared with macOS, so it waits for the owner.

findings.title: The SEP's SLEEP message decoded; test R18 built, not armed
findings.body: cmsgSLEEP's 8-byte message is 0x000c0000 with the sleep type in byte 3 (EP 0, op 0x0c, param 2, data 0); its u32 argument is the reply timeout (15 s outside simulators), not data. The J414s SEP node has a single always-on domain (ps_sep), so the driver holds nothing extra. apple_sep.test_sleep_msg (default 0) sends it at PM_SUSPEND_PREPARE; run R18 = R17 + type 2. The module is not installed until the owner answers.

findings.title: SIO, MTP and the SEP run into every commit awake; macOS sleeps every IOP through RTBuddy
findings.body: macOS's trace covered only the SMC and the PMP. In macOS, RTBuddy::setPowerState puts every RTKit coprocessor to sleep at system sleep. At our commit Linux has told the SMC, PMP and AOP (0x201) and shut the DCPs down, but the SEP, SIO (sio_suspend is a TODO stub) and MTP (rtkit-helper, built in, no PM ops) get nothing. apple_sio.test_sleep_idle (default off) sends RTKit IDLE 0x201 in .suspend; run R19 = R17 + that.

findings.title: SIO IDLE before the commit: still the 86 s reset (R19)
findings.body: Run R19 (image 60h, aura-ctl 0x1db1f, apple_sio.test_sleep_idle=Y, 2026-11-07 07:43): echo mem to the next kernel 85 s, PMU scratch identical to R17 (code 0x16). The SIO's ack is not visible: the kmsg stream stops before the device .suspend phase and the journal is lost. A normal-path run (S9) is to confirm the SIO accepts IDLE.

findings.title: The SIO acks RTKit IDLE; it is not what the entry waits for (S9)
findings.body: Run S9 (normal path, 2026-11-07 07:51): apple-sio 'TEST: firmware IDLE for system sleep: 0', back on the alarm in 32.4 s with all CPUs. With R19 (same step before the commit, still 86 s) the SIO is ruled out. Left: the SEP (R18, waits for the owner), MTP (built into the kernel), the GPU.

findings.title: maralcbr's post-slpa writes: most are already in Aura; the cluster APSC disable is new
findings.body: A static second pass (2026-11-07) over the trace's 74 writes. Aura's CLOCKS (ClkGen-SOC, T6000 offsets +4), PLL-off (0x28e224000, same sequence), CLUSTERS/EACC (soc-cluster words, T6000 at +0x10000) and DOMAINS (ps_sio_cpu AUTO_ENABLE) steps match the trace entry for entry, independently of our macOS 13.5 J414s RE. The PCIe write is in config space on T6020, the four die-quadrant error-handler writes fall outside every J414s reg, and the pmgr_dcp/PMP-report pre-slpa words sit in a window whose layout differs between chips: none are replayed. The J414s ADT turns APSC on (cpu-apsc = 1) and leaves the ppt/llc/amx throttles off, so the trace's one new cluster write is APSC_DIS (bit 23 on T6020, bit 22 on T6000). Image 61 adds it (run R20).

findings.title: Cluster APSC off before the release IPIs hangs the SoC; the S2R timer does not reset (R20)
findings.body: Run R20 (image 61, aura-ctl 0x3db1f, 2026-11-07 08:28): code 0x16 reached, but only Aura cpus 4 and 8 reached their S2R sleep (never-slept feee; cpu1 CPU_OFF, park-loop WFI never returned, a second IPI did not wake it), PCPM0 stayed on (0x6014 ff), and for the first time the timer did not reset the SoC: it hung until the owner held power 28 min later. R13 had an awake core and still reset at 86 s, so the APSC disable itself seems to block the timer's reset. macOS disables APSC only after its secondaries sleep; a variant after the snapshot (R20b) is possible but owner-present only. R18 (SEP SLEEP) runs first.

findings.title: The SEP SLEEP message is acknowledged but not what the entry waits for (R18)
findings.body: Run R18 (2026-11-07 09:27, R17 + apple_sep.test_sleep_msg=2): the enclave replied (tag 0x11, data 0), and the run ended in the same 86 s timer reset with PMU scratch identical to R17's. macOS 15.6.1 then clears the SEP mailbox OUTBOX_CTRL enable and writes 0x1000030f to the SEP's PMGR word (PS_AUTO 0, so the PMGR may gate the enclave); J414s ps_sep reads 0x1f0000ff (PS_AUTO f, never gated). R18B adds that step; built, waits for the owner to be present.

findings.title: Three fabric lanes (and the SEP) are never allowed to auto-gate on J414s; macOS sets their floor to 0
findings.body: From maralcbr's T6000 sleep-entry PMGR dump mapped by DT label: AFNC1_LW2, AFNC2_LW1, APCIE_GP_SYS and SEP read 0x1f0000ff on J414s (AUTO_ENABLE, PS_AUTO f), macOS has 0x1000030f (PS_AUTO 0) at sleep entry; AFNC3_LW0 already matches. Linux's pmgr-pwrstate never writes PS_AUTO. Image 62 (run R21) and R18B test it.

rules: Never remove and rescan PCI devices: it kills Wi-Fi until a reboot.
No `slpa` runs unless the owner is ready to reset the Mac by hand.
Keep a `.keep` file in module trees pacman doesn’t own.
No hotplug tests on a boot that can hurt the root filesystem.
Check the ESP sha after every copy, and refuse to suspend on the default image.
Test GRUB entries use `panic=0`, so a panic hangs and the watchdog stamps tell where it died.
unknowns: Whether iBoot arms the wake path (reconfig engine, boot CPU RVBAR) for a raw image as it does for a kernelcache.
What starts the SoC’s sleep: not `slpa` alone (the PMGR counters stay in `AWAKE`); presumably the PMGR’s S2R entry, which Aura does not do yet. And what restarts the AP on wake, through which RVBAR.
What the reconfig engine runs on `SLP_S2R`, and what each quiesce action writes.
Whether a DCP with nothing attached can be shut down and restarted.
What the PMP’s VLPM tunables control.
Why an inline `dsb sy; isb; wfi` in `SYSTEM_SUSPEND` never woke when `deep_wfi()` does.
Whether the PMP accepts IDLE after `slpa` once it is sent once (run C again), and whether it needs its display requests released first
What the ANS waits for after `slpa`: it answers HELLO but never acks IOP power-on (likely the storage power the SMC only restores in a real S2R wake)
